question: Solve for video recording — an adversary records the screen for the whole reading session.
headline: It cannot be solved in software, and the reason is a two-line argument. With one cheap physical element at the reader it CAN be solved against ordinary cameras, exactly and provably. It still cannot be solved against a camera that isolates individual display frames.

necessity_argument.claim: No display-only scheme can prevent recovery from a complete recording.
necessity_argument.proof: If the display is a function of the document and time alone, the reader's retina integrates incident light over some window W to give R(W). The adversary holds every frame, so the adversary can compute R(W) for any W including the reader's. Anything legible to the reader is therefore legible to the adversary.
necessity_argument.consequence: The escape is forced: the reader must hold a physical element that makes their optical path differ from the camera's, so the two integrate different subsequences.

construction.hardware: shutter glasses synchronised to the display; the reader sees a 50% duty cycle, so the panel runs brighter to compensate
construction.cycle: four frames at 240 Hz — A = L+d and B = L-d are passed; X = (1-L)+e and Y = (1-L)-e are blocked
construction.identity_1: (A+B)/2 = L exactly — the reader sees the true page
construction.identity_2: (A+B+X+Y)/4 = 1/2 exactly, pixel by pixel, independently of the masks, because L + (1-L) = 1 everywhere
construction.measured_uniformity: max deviation of the full-cycle average from 0.5 was 5.55e-17 (floating-point exact)
construction.meaning: a capture spanning whole cycles contains no spatial information at all — not degraded information, none

what_it_does_not_defeat.attack: frame-resolved capture then pairwise frame search
what_it_does_not_defeat.cost: 28 OCR trials found the complementary pair (0,2); scoring candidates by 'does this read as text' is trivial, so a keyed frame schedule buys nothing

what_it_does_not_defeat.attack: single isolated blocked frame, unmask then invert
what_it_does_not_defeat.note: the photographic negative of a page is exactly as readable as the page

why_single_frame_security_is_impossible: Mask amplitude is bounded by display headroom, and headroom trades directly against the content contrast the reader needs. At any human-readable contrast the per-frame signal-to-mask ratio is about 1, and OCR beats that by aggregating over a glyph's many pixels. Reducing content contrast to widen the mask reduces it for the reader too, because the reader sees the average.
practical_boundary: The construction defeats any camera whose exposure spans two or more display frames, which covers auto-exposure video and auto-exposure photography of a screen. It falls to a deliberately short manual shutter (about 1/500 s or faster at 240 Hz) combined with a per-frame unmasking attack. That is a real rise in required effort and equipment, and it is not security.
what_actually_holds_for_video: Aperture bounding: cap what any capture can contain. Measured 0.053-0.067 true-content recovery per capture at 12-60 character apertures, needing 33-165 captures for one page. The bound is on information present in the frame, so no image processing reaches it.
Per-session frame watermarking: a recording is attributable to the session and device even when it is readable.
Rate limiting: the leak is bounded by the reading rate and the session length, both observable and loggable.
Camera-lens detection by retroreflection, as used in cinemas, for a controlled-room tier. Real technology, not software, and not deployable to a laptop in a cafe.
honest_summary: The camera-pointed-at-a-screen case, which is precisely the case operating-system capture exclusion cannot touch, is now closed against ordinary equipment with an exact zero-information guarantee. The high-speed-camera case does not close, and the argument above shows it never will by concealment. For that case the answer is bounding and attribution, which is the same answer the rest of this project gives.
